headline: A 2016 law that changes how federal inspectors general operate, their access to records, their reporting duties, and how complaints against them are handled.
what_it_does: The law exempts inspectors general from certain privacy and paperwork rules when they conduct audits and investigations. It sets rules for how the Council of the Inspectors General on Integrity and Efficiency handles complaints against inspectors general, including deadlines for referrals and investigations. It requires inspectors general to include more detail in their semiannual reports and gives them a process for requesting federal grand jury materials, which the Justice Department can deny only for listed reasons.

who_it_affects.how: They gain exemptions from certain privacy and paperwork requirements during authorized oversight work and must follow new reporting, referral, and recommendation rules.

who_it_affects.group: Federal agencies overseen by inspectors general
who_it_affects.how: Agencies must respond to inspector general requests for records and grand jury materials, and their unresolved recommendations must be listed in inspector general reports.
Inspectors general must report retaliation against whistle-blowers, but they may not reveal a whistle-blower's personal information without consent.

who_it_affects.group: Senior federal employees accused of misconduct
who_it_affects.how: Substantiated misconduct investigations involving senior employees must be described in inspector general semiannual reports.

who_it_affects.group: Special Counsel and Deputy Special Counsel of the Office of Special Counsel
who_it_affects.how: The oversight council may now receive, review, and refer wrongdoing allegations against these officials.

who_it_affects.group: Members of Congress and congressional committees
who_it_affects.how: They receive semiannual reports, corrective action recommendations, and investigation reports from the oversight council.
It must decide requests from inspectors general for grand jury materials and explain any denial to Congress.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 16, 2016; the summary does not list any other effective dates.
